questions.question: Using valence bond theory, explain the formation of sigma and pi bonds in ethene, C₂H₄. State the hybridisation of each carbon atom and the H–C–H bond angle.
questions.solution:
**Step 1 — Structure.**

Each carbon in C₂H₄ has 4 valence electrons; one is used in a double bond and three in single bonds, so each carbon is bonded to three other atoms. Steric number = 3, hence each carbon is **sp² hybridised**.

**Step 2 — Sigma bonds.**

Three sp² hybrids on each carbon lie in one plane at $120^\circ$ to each other. Two of them overlap with the 1s orbitals of H atoms (C–H σ bonds) and the third overlaps head-on with an sp² hybrid of the other carbon.

$$\text{Total } \sigma \text{ bonds} = 4(\text{C–H}) + 1(\text{C–C}) = 5 \ \sigma \text{ bonds}$$

**Step 3 — Pi bond.**

Each carbon retains one unhybridised 2p orbital perpendicular to the plane. These two orbitals overlap sideways (laterally) to form one π bond.

$$\text{Total } \pi \text{ bonds} = 1$$

Hence the C=C double bond = 1 σ + 1 π. All six atoms are coplanar and $\angle \text{H–C–H} = 120^\circ$. Rotation about the C=C bond is restricted because it would break the π bond.
questions.knowledgeNote: In ethene each sp² carbon forms three σ bonds, and one unhybridised 2p orbital forms the single π bond.
